content:
The test image shows a corn stalk split open longitudinally. Key features:
- Pith completely disintegrated/shredded into fibrous vascular strands
- Pale gray-tan/white coloration throughout
- No pink/red discoloration (rules out Gibberella/Fusarium)
- No obvious black sclerotia (would suggest Charcoal rot)
- Dry, fibrous shredded appearance

This pattern strongly suggests a stalk rot. The pale tan/white shredded pith points toward Diplodia Stalk Rot. Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference shows Diplodia stalk rot with external collapse/lodging. The test image shows a split stalk interior with completely shredded, fibrous pale tan/gray pith — classic internal stalk rot presentation.

Comparing features:
- Pale tan/gray color (not pink = rules out Gibberella/Fusarium; not black = rules out Charcoal rot)
- Completely disintegrated pith leaving only vascular fiber strands
- Dry, hollow appearance

This is consistent with **Diplodia Stalk Rot**, where the pith bleaches to white/tan and shreds into fibers as the fungus destroys internal tissue.
